title: Late neurons write output tokens: their job is readable as the words they push
detail: 68% of the top-5 neurons in 4,194 concept maps sit in layers 28-35 (run 1). 'Say' neurons put their effect on the answer directly (direct share 1.05). Forcing one neuron hard gives a consistent word list only here (91-100% consistent across backgrounds vs 2-36% in layers 0-23). Late fact neurons act at the answer position, not at the subject.

title: Early neurons do not write words; they work through later neurons
detail: Direct effect on the answer 0.00 for 516 early key neurons. Zeroing an early key neuron cuts a later 'say' neuron's activation by 11.7% vs ~0 for an activation-matched null (312 pairs, p < 1e-50). No consistent forced word output even at 16x its peak.

title: A concept's key neurons form a feed-forward assembly; late neurons are its readable end
detail: Every type of key neuron feeds later key neurons of the same concept (early -> say, attribute -> say, say -> later say; all p < 1e-5), mostly within the answer position and about a fifth between words through a small set of heads. The answer is staged at layers 28-29 at the turn boundary.

title: Early layers (median layer 8) hold entity-specific neurons that act at the entity's own name tokens
detail: 86 entities (landmarks, people, works; 333 facts): neurons ranked by attribution over only the name tokens across all layers, then zeroed only there. Of the top-3 per entity with drop > 0.2 (218 neurons): median layer 8, 89% below layer 20; 96% are >= 5x more specific to their own entity than to others.

title: ...but early entity neurons are broad on the input side and partly shared
detail: Their web-text firings are mostly not about their entity (median 5%); 55% also matter causally for at least one other entity, coherently at layers 7-13 (Renaissance paintings, literary epics, bridges). Polysemantic on input, specific in use.

title: Mid-to-late neurons include relation neurons that act at the answer position
detail: 45% of layer 20-27 fact neurons are relation neurons (255 overall across 11 relations). Cleanest example: L30:8291 ('century built') costs ~3.2 log-odds on the century fact of every landmark tested and nothing on their other facts.

title: Fact knowledge looks like a factorised lookup: entity (early) x relation (mid-late) -> shared value neurons (late)
detail: Answer-value neurons are shared by every fact with the same answer (e.g. a '19th century' neuron across four landmarks); the entity -> value route is causal and specific but distributed (top-1 entity neuron explains 2.2% of the value neuron).

title: Layers ~16-24 host shared answer-format machinery
detail: 35 neurons in 16-24 fire for every concept; the most widely shared (hundreds of concepts, e.g. L20:7473) are fed by the same upstream neurons whatever the concept and drive 'Title-Case term' neurons at layers 24-25. Specific to the 'Answer with just the name' format.

title: Concept neurons help on their own topic in ordinary text only in late layers
detail: Switching a concept neuron off on its own topic hurts next-token prediction in layers 24-35 (+0.004-0.005 nats/token), not earlier. Single-firing effects are only ~1.5x bf16 noise.

title: Layers 20-27 are a genuine mix with no single job
detail: Relation extraction, task/format machinery and intermediate composition; little readable output of their own. All bands are bins over a gradient, not hard boundaries.

title: Turn-boundary copier: the top carrier of a concept's assembly between words
detail: A top cross-position carrier in 173 of 312 concepts. With the next carriers (L31H3, L34H21, L26H20, L35H22), patching the top-3 heads recovers 56% of the between-word composition vs 0% for random heads.

title: Late turn-boundary copier carrying the staged answer
detail: One of the shared carriers of the assembly between words (cross-position study); copies the answer staged at the turn boundary.

title: Shared carrier of concept assemblies between words
detail: Second most frequent cross-position carrier after L34H28 (cross-position study, 312 concepts).

title: Shared carrier of concept assemblies between words
detail: Among the most frequent cross-position carriers (cross-position study, 312 concepts).

title: Mid-layer meaning carrier
detail: Carries concept information between words in the middle of the network; also a top cross-position carrier.

title: Mid-layer meaning carrier
detail: Named with L26H20 as a mid-layer meaning carrier of the assembly between words (LAYERS_AND_JOBS S3; attention study).

title: Relation neuron: 'century built'
detail: Costs ~3.2 log-odds on the century fact of every landmark tested and nothing on their other facts.

title: Era neuron: '19th century' = 18xx, across answer formats
detail: Raises '19th century' and 18xx years whichever format the question asks for (numeric facts study, 18 Oct).
